response.consequence: A permission granted after a denial can stay denied until the short TTL expires. That is a freshness trade-off, not an authorization bypass.
response.explanation: The denial cache is only read to return a deny, and it is only written when the permission check returns not-allowed. The key includes the namespace, user UID, action, name and parent folder. An allow result is never cached for reuse. The cached-permission path uses the same keys as the DB path. A failed lookup falls through to the DB path, and only an explicit allow short-circuits the check. Unsupported identity types still return an error. The in-process client now uses NoopCache, which disables client-side caching. The remote client keeps its local cache as before. I found no input that can cross the trust boundary.
